title: Strided KV slab-slicing and per-head token-tiling hints for multi-head QA (GQA/MQA)
author: Marcus Li
description: Motivation: certain MQA/GQA model variants show pathological latency when KV cache layout and kernel tiling are misaligned with head-stride and token packing patterns. This PR introduces a lightweight runtime hinting layer that computes per-model and per-run strided KV slab-slicing parameters and per-head token-tiling alignments. The goal is to reduce atomic memory scatter and improve coalesced loads for multihead quantized models (especially 4-bit MQA and some Llama Mistral forks) while preserving stable latency for small batch workloads. Changes: 1) add KVCacheStridePolicy which derives an initial slab size and slice stride from model config + observed sequence distribution, 2) implement a slab-slicer that maps logical KV indices to physical slab offsets with optional padding to head-aligned boundaries, 3) inject token-tiling hints into kernel selection so backend can choose planar vs interleaved kernels based on head alignment, 4) add a short-circuit fallback for tiny batches (<8 tokens) to avoid over-splitting, 5) instrument counters and histograms exposed to the Console for slab hits, misalignment penalties, and fallback activations. Benchmarks and safety: microbenchmarks on p4d (A100 equiv) and a small rtx cluster show median token latency improvements of 8-15% on MQA-4 models for long-context (>1024) chat workloads and 3-6% improvement for Llama-2 variants using GQA packing. No accuracy/regression impact observed in deterministic evals. Rollout plan: feature gated by model-profile opt-in and controlled rollout with canary on 5% of production traffic initially. Checklist: [x] unit tests for slab-slicer math, [x] integration tests exercising fallback path, [x] telemetry added to Console, [x] docs stub for runtime hints, [x] performance regression run attached. Related: ENG-7542, ENG-7699. Why unique: complements existing kernel-routing work by providing a compact runtime-level mapping that reduces misaligned memory ops without changing core kernels; intended as an incremental, reversible heuristic rather than a permanent model transform.

benchmarks: Microbenchmarks: MQA-4 long-context median token latency down 12% (p95 down 9%). Llama-2 GQA packing median token latency down 5%. Small-batch (<8) unchanged or slightly better due to fallback. End-to-end cost estimate: ~4% token-cost savings for high-concurrency chat workloads with long context.
